data.body:
This bundle is for people who use AI at work. It gives you three pieces: a guide to setting Claude up so you stop re-explaining yourself in every chat, a set of 14 Specialists with 231 prompts to start from, and a set of rules you load once so your AI follows them.

The Claude Operator’s Manual

I wrote this Manual for Claude users who want to run Claude well. It is a 217-page PDF about Claude only.

  • Set up Claude in the app. Start with the day-one setup checklist in the appendices. The first half covers talking to Claude well, setting up Projects and knowledge files, Skills, and connecting Claude to the tools your work lives in, and they need no terminal.
  • Go further with Claude Code. The Claude Code chapters are optional, and they are the only ones that ask you to open a terminal.
  • Copy complete workflows. The last part puts the setup together into workflows you can reuse.
  • Check your work. Every chapter ends with a checklist.

Your Personal Specialists

A Specialist is a setup message you paste into your AI, plus prompts for the problems in its area. Bring a problem to the right Specialist and paste your prompt. This is a 72-page PDF with 14 Specialists and 231 prompts, with brackets for your own details. Set each Specialist up once in the AI you already use: the guide shows how to set each one up in ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or Grok. The 14 Specialists are Marketing, Sales, Finance, Operations, HR, Customer Service, Content, Data, Project Management, Executive Assistant, Product, Legal and Compliance, Small Business, and Freelancer and Consultant.

Standing Orders for Your AI

A set of 20 rules you load into your AI once, so it follows them in every chat. Each rule can be switched on or off, and you can set the strength to Light, Standard or Full. For example, rule 1 is “Never make things up.” At Light, your AI says so when it isn’t sure a fact is right. At Full, it gives no fact without a source you can check. A guide shows how to load the rules into ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini and Grok, and another shows how to edit them.

Prices are in US dollars.

data.heading: Why the Specialists work
paras: A common reason a prompt fails is that the AI does not know your situation, so it guesses. You get a confident, generic answer that fits nobody.
Each Specialist starts with a setup you paste once. The setup tells the AI to ask before it guesses. So when you skip the details, it does one of two things:

1. It interviews you. You get a few short questions about what it needs: who it is for, what you have tried, what a good result looks like. You answer in a line or two, and the next reply fits your situation.
  2. It drafts with the gaps marked. You get a usable draft with [PLACEHOLDERS] where your facts belong, and it tells you what to fill in. Nothing invented sits in your draft looking like a fact.

I ran the setups in Gemini and Grok. In both, a prompt sent without context came back as one of those two replies. The tool changed. The behaviour did not. You do not need to write a perfect prompt: paste the setup, paste the prompt, answer what it asks.

data.heading: See it happen: Sales Specialist

turns.text: The Sales Specialist setup, then: “Write a cold email to Priya Shah, Operations Director at Northline Freight. My product: scheduling software for delivery fleets. The specific pain I solve: dispatchers lose time re-planning routes by hand. Keep it under 100 words, avoid jargon, end with a specific call to action, and include a subject line. Use only what I tell you about Northline Freight.”

Before I draft, four quick questions:

  1. Is this a first contact with Priya, or has she replied to you before?
  2. Do you want pricing in the email, or should it wait for a call?
  3. What should Priya do next: book a call, reply, or watch a short demo?
  4. Who is sending it, and what is your name and title?
Marcus, I run Halcyon Routing, a four-person software company. First contact, nothing from her yet. Leave pricing out. I want a 15-minute call.

Subject: Dispatch re-planning, one idea for Northline

Hi Priya,

Dispatchers often lose hours when a stop changes. Halcyon Routing builds scheduling software for delivery fleets, so your dispatchers spend less time re-planning routes by hand.

We are a small team, so I would rather show you than describe it. Are you free for a 15-minute call on Tuesday at 10 am?

Marcus
Halcyon Routing

data.note: The AI asked only what it could not know, and the draft stayed inside the facts Marcus gave.
